newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post - April 15.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on its front page on April 15:
WASHINGTON - Attorney General Janet Reno rejected Republican demands for an independent counsel to investigate reports of illegal fund-raising by the 1996 Clinton re-election campaign.

LITTLE ROCK, ARKANSAS - James McDougal, a former partner with the Clintons in the failed Whitewater real estate land venture, was sentenced to three years in prison after the Whitewater special counsel asked for a reduced sentenced.
NEW YORK - Fifty years after Jackie Robinson integrated professional baseball, the places where he lived and played are islands of racial division.

WASHINGTON - Some Army drill sergeants at Aberdeen Proving Ground kept lists of female trainees they had sex with, passed the names among themselves and, in one case, allegedly used the information to blackmail a woman, according to court testimony, Army officials and court documents.
WASHINGTON - Scientists have new evidence that challenges the notion that the earliest Americans resembled today's Asians.

WASHINGTON - The Supreme Court rejected an appeal that contended federal sentencing laws discriminate against blacks by punishing people caught with crack cocaine more severely than those caught with the drug in a powder form.

SEOUL, SOUTH KOREA - The South Korean government, in an effort to curb the vast sums of money families spend on private lessons, has banned such tutoring in any subject offered during the regular school day except art and music.
